name: Binding Invoker
description:
Invoke one named binding of a supplied OpenBindings interface document, read under the exact kind of the source the binding names. invokeBinding exchanges the described input and output frames; no native invocation handle is part of this interface. A kind may be defined in writing, privately or in code.

These operations are offered for voluntary adoption by name. Their schemas and descriptions identify the exchanged values and the capability they describe; they do not prescribe an SDK, internal algorithm, validation or recovery policy, or process architecture. Correspondence is an author claim, not verification of an implementation.

The source's kind gives the source's data and the binding's data their meaning. The invoker reads the binding's data, its source's data and whatever those refer to, as the kind defines, and nothing else on the kind's behalf. It selects no binding and validates no values. Data preserves absence versus JSON null. The open document schema is not a complete document-conformance check. Admission of malformed documents is implementation policy; it does not make those documents conformant.

BindingContext.description: Opaque context supplied by value for one attempt, as the context document defines it. Its members are whatever a previous challenge's schema described or the caller knows the source's kind reads; this interface defines none of them, requires no store, and prescribes no acquisition mechanism. How a value is used stays inside the kind's implementation. A value may be secret: a challenge marks secrets writeOnly, and callers avoid disclosing context through logs, diagnostics or storage keys.

ContextRequiredDetails.description: The data of a CONTEXT_REQUIRED error or a preflight result, as the context document defines it: why the attempt could not proceed, in the producer's words, and a JSON Schema of the context object to supply on the next attempt. The schema is ordinary JSON Schema 2020-12: oneOf branches with a title each for alternatives, required for values needed together, writeOnly on secrets, and a property description for where a person obtains a value. It describes the context requested for one attempt, not permission to disclose anything else. Acquisition, trust, storage and retry decisions belong to the caller.

message.description: Why the attempt could not proceed, in the producer's words, for a person to read.

schema.description: A JSON Schema 2020-12 schema, in object form, of the context object to supply on the next attempt. The context document defines the conventions it uses and the oauth2 annotation an application may act on.

InvocationError.description: Unsuccessful-completion record carried by an error frame. The frame kind signals failure independently of the code. Codes defined by the invocation interfaces retain their documented meanings; kind-defined codes have that kind's meaning, and other strings have implementation-specific meaning. ERR_REFUSED asserts no observable effect of the requested operation; CONTEXT_REQUIRED additionally carries the context challenge and asserts no operation output. ERR_EXECUTION_FAILED reports failure without a claim about effects, dispatch, blame, retryability or protocol category. Choosing whether to trust or act on an error is consumer policy.

code.description: Machine-readable reason. Binding invocation owns ERR_BINDING_NOT_FOUND (the requested key names no binding in the supplied interface), CONTEXT_REQUIRED (context requested, no operation output or effects), ERR_REFUSED (no operation effects), ERR_EXECUTION_FAILED (failure making no claim about effects or dispatch), ERR_FRAME_PROTOCOL (reported frame-exchange violation), ERR_TRANSPORT_CLOSED (transport ended before a terminal outcome), and ERR_CANCELLED (caller cancellation, with no rollback or external-stop claim). Operation invocation additionally owns ERR_OPERATION_NOT_FOUND (unresolved operation), ERR_BINDING_SELECTION_REQUIRED (ambiguous binding choice), ERR_OPERATION_VALIDATION_FAILED (value violates a declared schema), and ERR_SCHEMA_UNRESOLVED (validity could not be determined), and also reports ERR_BINDING_NOT_FOUND with a broader meaning (unresolved allowed binding). These meanings do not prescribe detection, recovery or precedence. Other codes have kind-defined or implementation-specific meanings.

data.description: Optional portable JSON data associated with the unsuccessful completion. A rule defining `code` may define its structure and semantics; otherwise, the source's kind may use it to preserve an opaque application-authored failure value. For CONTEXT_REQUIRED, this is a ContextRequiredDetails object. Presence is significant: an absent member means no portable associated value, while an explicit null is a present JSON null value. Statuses, headers, trailers, envelopes, raw debugging bytes, exception prose, stacks, and implementation evidence do not belong here unless they are themselves application data under an explicit governing rule.

BindingInvocationInput.description: Initial open-frame payload: the interface document, the key of the binding to invoke in it, and context to apply.

binding.description: Key of the binding to invoke in interface. A key that names no binding in interface is ERR_BINDING_NOT_FOUND.

BindingInvokerInputFrame.description: Caller messages: open introduces the invocation request, input carries a value and close ends caller input. The exchange begins with one open; close is optional when input or invocation has already ended. Repeated close has the same meaning. Handling messages outside the described exchange is implementation policy.

oneOf.title: open
oneOf.description: Open the invocation. MUST be the first frame on the input stream.

oneOf.title: input
oneOf.description: Write one input value to the underlying binding. The value's schema is determined by the underlying binding's operation, not by this contract.

oneOf.title: close
oneOf.description: Caller half-close: no further input values. It does not itself report operation completion. Repetition has the same meaning.

BindingInvokerOutputFrame.description: One frame from the service back to the caller. The service streams a sequence: zero or more non-terminal frames (`output`, `input_closed`) followed by exactly one terminal frame (`complete` or `error`).

oneOf.title: output
oneOf.description: One output value from the underlying binding. The value's schema is determined by the underlying binding's operation, not by this contract.

oneOf.title: input_closed
oneOf.description: The invoked binding is no longer accepting input. This is not a terminal outcome; outputs may still follow. Handling subsequent caller frames is implementation policy.

oneOf.title: complete
oneOf.description: Terminal: the underlying binding completed normally. MUST be the last frame.

oneOf.title: error
oneOf.description: Terminal: the underlying binding failed. MUST be the last frame. Carries a structured InvocationError.

openbindings.binding-invoker.invokeBindi.description:
Invoke the named binding of the supplied interface document and exchange caller-facing values as the kind of the binding's source defines. The invoker reads the binding's data, the data of the source it names and whatever those refer to, and nothing else on the kind's behalf; in particular, it does not read the operation declaration. Adaptation that needs an operation's schemas is expressed in binding data, which may refer to them. The invoker selects no binding and validates no values. A key that names no binding in the document is ERR_BINDING_NOT_FOUND. The caller may send a smaller document that preserves the binding's meaning.

The caller sends an open frame carrying the invocation request, followed by input frames and an optional close. close means no further input values; input_closed reports that the invoked binding is no longer accepting input. Repeated close has the same meaning. A caller close is unnecessary when input has already closed or the invocation has ended. The service returns output and input_closed frames followed by one terminal complete or error. complete reports successful completion; error reports unsuccessful completion. No further frames belong to the invocation after its terminal frame. An output value alone does not report success. A late failure does not retract values already delivered or assert that no effects occurred.

Frame schemas describe the messages. Handling malformed frames, late inputs or interrupted transports is implementation policy; ERR_FRAME_PROTOCOL and ERR_TRANSPORT_CLOSED identify those reported failures. The interface does not prescribe parser order, buffer admission, internal terminal-race arbitration, queue draining, polling or handle disposal. ERR_CANCELLED reports cancellation without promising rollback or that external work has stopped.

CONTEXT_REQUIRED carries ContextRequiredDetails, the context document's challenge: why the attempt could not proceed and a JSON Schema of the context to supply on the next attempt. It means that the attempt produced neither operation output nor observable effects of the requested operation; this meaning also applies if supplied context proved unusable. The caller may acquire what the schema describes and make another attempt; the signal does not require or authorize automatic replay. The interface supplies no store, acquisition mechanism, trust decision or retry policy.

ERR_REFUSED means the requested operation had no observable effects; ERR_EXECUTION_FAILED makes no such claim. Other error codes retain the meanings described for them or by their defining kind. The interface does not prescribe how an implementation determines these outcomes.

openText.description: One opening frame that runs repeatText in the illustrative text document. Under example.text@1, binding data echo returns the input string. Further input/output and a terminal outcome belong to this exchange.

count.description: Count Unicode code points in the input string.

textValue.description: Individual value frames within that exchange; not the whole invocation.

completion.description: One possible successful terminal outcome. A preceding output value alone would not report success.

contextChallenge.description: A separate illustrative protected service asks for an access token. This terminal outcome claims no operation output or effects; the schema describes what to supply on the next attempt, not permission to disclose anything else. Whether and how to make another attempt is the caller's choice.

data.message: The text service needs an access token.

accessToken.description: A bearer token for the text service.

openbindings.binding-invoker.preflightBi.description: Report context requirements identifiable for a possible invocation, as ContextRequiredDetails, or null for no prediction. Preflight does not perform the requested operation, consume its inputs or produce its outputs. It is advisory: null is a valid result even when invocation will need context; invocation does not depend on prior preflight. An unsuccessful completion reports inability to answer; ERR_REFUSED additionally reports that the same request would be refused without operation effects. Acquiring what the binding's data and its source's data refer to, caching and other preparation are implementation choices under the source's kind.
